invariants: T-001 one tenant_id identifies exactly one Tenant
T-003 a Tenant belongs to exactly one Platform Instance
T-004 this component is the authoritative source of Tenant state
T-005 transitions are limited to the published state machine
T-008 disallowed lifecycle states block ordinary tenant-scoped operations
T-009 no component gets direct access to this store: a consumer is published the contract reads listed under api.consumer_surface and receives values only
T-011 operations carry the standard observability context

operations.purpose: provision a Tenant in this Platform Instance

consumer_surface.transport: tenant_authority.transport.open_channel + tenant_authority.transport.call_contract — the published HTTP contract executed in process over an opaque channel handle (ARCHITECTURE.md §1.1 interaction mode API, Level 0)
errors: tenant_authority.errors.TenantAuthorityError and its published subclasses, reconstructed from status code and machine-readable reason
tenant_authority.errors.ContractViolation — raised when the component answers outside its contract; a consumer must fail closed
guarantees: values only: no store handle, audit journal, idempotency table, engine reference or mutation operation is reachable through the published surface

the published client holds no callable: its state is a channel handle, a credential and a Platform Instance binding, so walking __closure__ and cell_contents of the client and of its class reaches neither the component's ASGI application nor its deployment, engine or store
the ASGI application is never handed out: it stays behind the provider-side channel table, and a channel is revoked when the consumer drops the client

importing the published module binds no reference to tenant_authority.transport — its namespace holds no module object, no channel table and no transport type, so the consumer surface is not a door to the internal executor
an unknown or revoked channel handle raises ContractViolation, so there is no permissive fallback and a handle cannot be guessed
every read is executed by the same routing, service-identity authentication, permission check, Platform Instance ownership validation and audit code that serves an HTTP request
the consuming service identity comes from the credential bound to the client and cannot be chosen by the caller
an answer outside the published contract raises tenant_authority.errors.ContractViolation, so a consumer fails closed instead of assuming that the Tenant is servable
composition_root_only: the contract application itself (the ASGI application) — a consumer component must not own or re-export it
the contract channel table tenant_authority.transport._CHANNELS — a handle-to-application mapping owned by the component; a consumer receives a handle and never a transport object
consumer_surface.note: The deployment object is composition-internal: it assembles engine, store and contract application for the composition root and for this component's own tests and is never handed to a consumer. There is no consumer-facing runtime API and no second Tenant Context mechanism. Publishing is a two-step act owned by the provider: the contract application is registered with tenant_authority.transport.open_channel, and the consumer receives the resulting handle wrapped in the client — never the application, never the transport.

denial_semantics.foreign_tenant_response: answered as tenant_not_found at the transport level; the precise reason remains in the audit journal

events.note: IS-002 does not publish inter-component events and does not simulate a broker. Tenant deletion as a contract-visible lifecycle event is deferred with the event infrastructure; `deleted` is a lifecycle state of the Tenant Registry here, not a data deletion engine.

data_export_cdc.note: No CDC or bulk export stream is implemented in IS-002.

ui.note: Class B Platform Service; tenant UI is an explicit non-goal of IS-002.

platform_id.description: Identifier of the Platform Instance this authority serves; the ownership check compares tenant.platform_id with this value.

notes: Tenant Registry is platform-scoped: it is data of one Platform Instance. Cross-tenant listing is permitted only as an explicitly authorized and audited platform-scoped operation (ARCHITECTURE.md §5.4, LAW-16a).
No dataset of this component is tenant-scoped: lifecycle state belongs to the Tenant as a whole and is required to decide whether tenant-scoped data may be served at all.

audit.journal: internal append-only journal owned by tenant_authority
audit.note: Audit is owned data, not a public event contract; it is reachable through GET /api/v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/transitions for lifecycle history.

authn.note: IS-002 is operated by services and operators of one Platform Instance; it proves the authority boundary and is not an IAM product.

compatibility_policy.lifecycle_states: adding a state or an allowed transition is a minor change; removing or redefining one is a breaking change
